extracted.intended_audience: librarians, children's book authors/illustrators, publishers, researchers and general readers interested in children's book awards
extracted.subtask_description: Historical and procedural information and (implicit) criteria for the Kate Greenaway Medal — the UK award recognising illustration in children's books, including shortlist practices and related honours (Amnesty CILIP/Shadowers' Choice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / scope of the Medal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Medal recognises the year's best work(s) of illustration for children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically the award is for illustration in children's books; examples across decades include picture books, retellings/adaptations, information books and later graphic novels. (Source phrasing from notes: 'recognising the year's best work(s) of illustration for children.')

rubrics_metrics.name: Commendations / Highly commended (historical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commendations and Highly commended runner-up distinctions were awarded historically but ceased to be awarded in 2003.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes there had been 99 such distinctions over 44 years and that 'Commendations ceased to be awarded in this year' (2003). This affects how runners-up were recognised before 2003.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlist size (typical and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2003 there have usually been eight books on the shortlist, but some years have had seven (and in one recent year six).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article records exceptions (e.g. 2004, 2008, 2014, 2018, 2023 had only seven; 2023 had six). Shortlist size is therefore a procedural feature that can vary year to year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award year / publication year convention (pre- and post-2007)
rubrics_metrics.description: After 2006 the awards year was adjusted. Before 2007 the year refers to when the book was published rather than when the medal was awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page explains: 'Before 2007 the year refers to when the book was published rather than when the medal was awarded i.e. the 2005 winner was announced and the medal presented in July 2006.' This is a procedural convention affecting dating of winners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amnesty CILIP Honour criteria (2016–2018)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional award, The Amnesty CLIP Honour, was bestowed upon a shortlisted entry in conjunction with Amnesty International for 'books that most distinctively illuminate, uphold or celebrate freedoms'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives the quoted purpose exactly: 'books that most distinctively illuminate, uphold or celebrate freedoms'. The honour was awarded 2016–2018 and is a topical/values-based adjunct to the Medal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shadowers' Choice Award (since 2019): selector and method
rubrics_metrics.description: The Shadowers' Choice Award is voted for and awarded by children and young people who shadow the Medals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduced in 2019 replacing the Amnesty CLIP Honour, this award's selection is based on votes by child/young-person 'shadowers' rather than the professional judging panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical eligibility practice: multiple-book recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically, the Medal was sometimes conferred upon an illustrator for multiple named books in a year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notes explain that in earlier decades (example: Papas commended for multiple years and other examples from the 1960s) an illustrator could be recognised for work across multiple books rather than a single title.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and type of works observed as eligible
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners and shortlisted works include a wide range of formats — picture books, retellings/adaptations, information books, editions of novellas, translated works and (more recently) graphic novels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited on the page: adaptations (Jonathan Swift's Gulliver), retellings (Cinderella, The Princess and the Pea), information/illustrated guides, translated works, and in 2022 Long Way Down (a graphic novel) won — indicating graphic novels and translations are eligible and have been successful.
